hypothesis: A deterministic source-to-decision report will improve research-heavy autonomy review by mapping watched agent and evaluation resources to local tasks, local decisions, explicit no-ops, and unmapped gaps without creating a parallel source catalog.

metricsCompared.name: focused source coverage tests
metricsCompared.baseline: no deterministic builder or CLI coverage for source-to-decision mapping
metricsCompared.candidate: source coverage and report CLI tests cover grouped text output, JSON output, stale warnings, no-op signals, local decisions, and task mappings

metricsCompared.name: operator rendered evidence
metricsCompared.baseline: watchlist-to-task and watchlist-to-decision coverage required manual grep across data and local guidance
metricsCompared.candidate: source-coverage-transcript.txt shows the report grouping adopted, open-task, rejected/no-op, and unmapped sources

metricsCompared.name: source catalog discipline
metricsCompared.baseline: future research task guidance did not name the source-to-decision disposition surfaces explicitly
metricsCompared.candidate: task guidance points future source dispositions at tasks, local AGENTS/docs, or watchlist snapshots without adding a second source catalog

rationale: The change is read-only report behavior over local watchlist, task, and decision data. Focused tests exercise deterministic mapping and CLI rendering, and the run transcript gives reviewer-visible output. The report flags gaps instead of creating tasks or fetching external sources, so it improves review evidence without changing workflow execution.
